title: Processes, Threads, and Memory Allocation
instructions: Answer from the lesson. For short-answer and practical items, equivalent technically correct wording/code earns credit.

questions.prompt: Which statement about threads in one process is generally true?

options.text: They share process memory but have separate execution stacks
They are different names for files

questions.explanation: Threads share process resources while maintaining separate execution state/stacks.

questions.prompt: What does process memory isolation primarily provide?

options.text: A guarantee that programs have no bugs
Separation of one process’s address space from another’s

questions.explanation: Virtual memory and OS enforcement isolate process address spaces.

questions.prompt: Two threads increment the same shared counter without synchronization. What risk exists?
questions.expected_answer: Interleaved reads and writes may cause updates to be lost; synchronization or atomic operations may be needed.
It supports isolation, mapping, and memory management; it is not simply the same thing as RAM.

questions.prompt: Give one reason to choose multiple processes over threads.
questions.expected_answer: Processes have more isolation, though communication and resource costs may be higher.
